entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Gerke et al. (2011), ApJ 743, 176, VizieR J/ApJ/743/176/table1 row M81C = 095610.62+690732.7: J2000 position; Gaia cannot see the star. Distance: Placed in M81 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 3,622,342 pc (src/objects/m81-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 3,614,099 pc, inclination 59 deg, line of nodes 150.2 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Newman2024ApJ...966..175N: An Empirical Calibration of the Tip of the Red Giant Branch Distance Method in the Near Infrared. I. Hubble Space Telescope WFC3/IR F110W and F160W Filters (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...966..175N); catalogue reference Newman2024ApJ...966..175N: 3614098.6264 pc (-65964.7340604/+33440.8428599); trgb (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...966..175N): 3622342 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star. Proper motion: J/ApJ/743/176/table1 row M81C = 095610.62+690732.7 measures no proper motion; zero is assumed (at 3,622,342 pc, 1 mas/yr would be 17,172 km/s across the sky). Radial velocity from SIMBAD's radial velocity of M81, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2022ApJS..261....6K; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured.

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 245.1 +/- 40.9 solar radii from Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 64.823 d in Gerke et al. (2011), ApJ 743, 176, VizieR J/ApJ/743/176/table1 M81C = 095610.62+690732.7 (Per); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.02186). No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4710 +/- 317 K from Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 64.823 d in Gerke et al. (2011), ApJ 743, 176, VizieR J/ApJ/743/176/table1 M81C = 095610.62+690732.7 (Per); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures.

entries.subject: Color
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at 4,710 K, because no archive holds a spectrum of this star (stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: the star is placed by a catalogue row, so no Gaia DR3 source is read for it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number), through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #ffe1c4. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: the star is placed by a catalogue row, so no Gaia DR3 source is read for it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number; planck: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 4,710 K and log g 0.6 (u1 0.710, u2 0.073): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.

entries.subject: Surface gravity
entries.finding: Unmeasured, bounded: no gravity of this star is published (none in SIMBAD); Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra) gives the class's range, log g -1.33 to 2.86. Across log g 0 to 2.85, the part the grid covers, the limb laws differ by at most 1.5% of the centre brightness from the one drawn, at log g 0.6, the gravity closest to all of them; log g 0.6 is a display choice, not a measurement.
